question.knowledge_point: Simplifying an Expression Using the Secant-Tangent and Other Identities
question.worked_solution:
First, let's recall the secant-tangent identity:

$$
1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x
$$

We rewrite the given expression using the secant-tangent identity as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{cos}^{2}⁡x\text{ }\,({sec}^{2}⁡x-2{tan}^{2}⁡x) & ={cos}^{2}⁡x\text{ }\,(1+{tan}^{2}⁡x-2{tan}^{2}⁡x) \\  & ={cos}^{2}⁡x(1-{tan}^{2}⁡x) \\  & ={cos}^{2}⁡x-{cos}^{2}⁡x\cdot {tan}^{2}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we recall the identities:

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x},\,{cos}^{2}⁡x=1-{sin}^{2}⁡x
$$

 

Using the above identities, we can further simplify our expression as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{cos}^{2}⁡x-{cos}^{2}⁡x\cdot {tan}^{2}⁡x & ={cos}^{2}⁡x-{cos}^{2}⁡x\cdot \frac{{sin}^{2}⁡x}{{cos}^{2}⁡x} \\  & ={cos}^{2}⁡x-\cancel{{cos}^{2}⁡x}\cdot \frac{{sin}^{2}⁡x}{\cancel{{cos}^{2}⁡x}} \\  & ={cos}^{2}⁡x-{sin}^{2}⁡x \\  & =1-{sin}^{2}⁡x-{sin}^{2}⁡x \\  & =1-2{sin}^{2}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
{cos}^{2}⁡x\text{ }\,({sec}^{2}⁡x-2{tan}^{2}⁡x)=1-2{sin}^{2}⁡x.
$$
